title: The 8 Levels of Reality Show Binges
house: A bustling metropolis of produce-people where glowing digital forehead numbers dictate social class, neon billboards flash streaming subscriptions, and every subway car features a gold coin hidden on the ads.
catchphrase: The forehead number never lies, but the watch history exposes your soul.
links: Level 2 baristas mention a brooding carrot customer who leaves massive tips.
Level 5 developer spots a glowing avocado missing her designer purse at the neon kiosk.
Level 8 executive remembers the quiet plum girl from the late shift.

gegenspieler.tat: Laughs loudly at her low binge-watch hours and labels her a basic amateur in front of the entire conference room.

levels.name: Pip, 24, Junior Assistant
levels.story: The 8 levels of reality show consumption. Level 1. Twelve hours a month on cheap reality shows—and my new boss just saw my browser tab! Twelve hours? That is rookie numbers around here, Pip. You are practically allergic to drama. I slouched behind my dual monitors at desks crowded with half-empty energy drinks in our fluorescent-lit open-plan office. How do you even function without crying over staged trash-TV breakups until 3 AM? I gripped my chipped ceramic mug tightly while searching for an escape route through the glass partitions. You will never survive the corporate elite with numbers like that. Brody had already planted a corrupted file in my local network folder just to humiliate me further. If you cannot explain this viewing drop by noon, your career here is officially over, Pip. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Toby, 29, Transit Dispatcher
levels.story: The 8 levels of reality show consumption. Level 2. Eighty-five hours a month—and my entire train car just heard my tablet blare the theme song. Eighty-five hours of garbage TV? Even the subway rats have better taste. I stood frozen in the packed underground carriage rattling beneath neon-drenched city streets while commuters stared at my orange-peel skin turning pale. Do you need a tissue for your fake tears, drama queen? I shoved my tablet into my canvas satchel, desperately wishing the subway floor would swallow me whole. Your secret playlist is about to be emailed to your entire department. The emergency brakes screeched violently, plunging the entire underground carriage into pitch blackness. Look at the central terminal screens! Everyone's watch history is being broadcast live to the city! You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Cleo, 26, Marketing Copywriter
levels.story: The 8 levels of reality show consumption. Level 3. One hundred ninety-five hours a month—and my CEO just caught me watching island makeout dramas during a budget review! Look at her eyes, she has not seen sunlight since the streaming age began. I slammed my laptop shut in the sleek glass boardroom overlooking the misty skyline while my avocado skin tingled with embarrassment. Is this what our marketing budget goes toward, or do you just fund your emotional breakdowns? I gripped the edges of my sleek mahogany chair, refusing to let my voice shake in front of the board of directors. Pack your desk by noon or your viewing history goes viral. The projector screen suddenly shifted to display a top-secret corporate directive overriding my terminal. The entire marketing division has been reassigned to manual data archiving in the basement. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Zack, 22, University Student
levels.story: The 8 levels of reality show consumption. Level 4. Three hundred forty-five hours a month—and my entire lecture hall is watching my live reaction to the season finale! Three hundred forty-five hours of garbage? Even my cat has a better GPA than you. I stood frozen in the middle of our crowded university amphitheater while my lemon-rind skin turned sour with humiliation. Are you actually taking notes on crying millionaires while organic chemistry finals are tomorrow? I slammed my backpack shut, scattering my lecture notes across the dusty wooden floorboards while students howled with laughter. Your professor just subscribed to your live reaction feed. Campus security suddenly bolted the heavy oak doors shut from the outside. Nobody leaves until the streaming algorithm completes its mandatory student behavior assessment. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Maya, 27, Independent Streamer
levels.story: The 8 levels of reality show consumption. Level 5. Five hundred forty-five hours a month—and my entire subscriber base just watched my rent check bounce live on stream! Five hundred forty-five hours of talking to empty chat rooms while your real life crumbles. I sat in my neon-lit streaming studio surrounded by ring lights and empty energy drink cans while my dragon-fruit scales flushed bright pink. Do you expect your fictional reality boyfriends to pay your electric bill when the power gets shut off? I clutched my streaming microphone tightly, fighting back tears as three thousand live viewers watched the disaster unfold. Your streaming studio lease has just been terminated by the landlord. A high-priority donation alert suddenly chimed across my audio monitoring software. Check your encrypted messages, Maya. The master network servers are wide open tonight. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Brody, 31, Reality Show Producer
levels.story: The 8 levels of reality show consumption. Level 6. Seven hundred ninety-five hours a month—and my own network executives just confiscated my master viewing pass! Seven hundred ninety-five hours of editing trash TV and you still cannot tell scripted drama from real life. I paced across the polished marble floor of our downtown broadcasting tower while my broccoli-floret hair bristled with pure rage. Are you really crying because the network cancelled your favorite trashy romance spinoff? I clenched my fists inside my tailored suit pockets, feeling my professional reputation evaporate into thin air. Your master archive access has been revoked by the board of directors. The central mainframe alarms wailed as the emergency purge countdown hit zero on all monitors. Sir, someone is deliberately uploading a master override file from the executive penthouse! You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Marcus, 35, Head of Network Syndication
levels.story: The 8 levels of reality show consumption. Level 7. One thousand ninety-five hours a month—and my entire media empire is crashing down because my viewing logs leaked! One thousand ninety-five hours of streaming addiction while running the biggest network in the country. I stood in my private penthouse office overlooking the glowing city skyline while my mango-skin turned a pale, sickly yellow. Do you expect the board to keep a network chief who spends more time watching trash TV than producing it? I gripped the edge of my custom glass desk, realizing my entire career had been built on a foundation of sand. Your resignation letter has already been sent to every major news outlet. The private elevator bell chimed softly as the security team blocked my escape route. Step away from the console, Marcus. The Supreme CEO is waiting upstairs. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Nicole, 42, Supreme Streaming CEO
levels.story: The 8 levels of reality show consumption. Level 8. Final Level. One thousand four-hundred fifty hours a month—and I am the one who scripted every single drama you ever watched! I whispered while gazing down at the entire glowing metropolis from my glass citadel. Every single fight, every broken engagement, every viral tear was engineered in this very room to feed your digital numbers. Cleo the Avocado stared up at me from the lower terrace, her 195-hour badge trembling beneath the flashing neon skyline. You built an entire society on judging people by their watch history. I adjusted my pristine white shell helmet, smiling as my digital forehead badge pulsed with absolute authority over every citizen below. My own forehead number began to flicker violently, exposing a hidden ninth tier deep within the master mainframe. Warning: Supreme Administrator session terminating. The viewers are now watching you. Who do you think is really watching your screen right now?
